questions.question: A quantity is measured in meters per second squared (m/s²). What is this quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** of an object with respect to **time**.
 
• The mathematical formula for **acceleration (a)** is expressed as the change in **velocity (Δv)** divided by the **time interval (Δt)**, represented as **a = Δv / Δt**.
 
• The **SI unit** for **velocity** is **meters per second (m/s)**, and the unit for **time** is **seconds (s)**. Therefore, the unit for **acceleration** is calculated as **(m/s) / s**, which simplifies to **m/s²** or **meters per second squared**.
 
• As a **vector quantity**, **acceleration** possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**, indicating how fast the velocity changes and in which direction the change occurs.
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, **acceleration** is directly proportional to the **net force** acting on an object and inversely proportional to its **mass** (**a = F/m**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force**:

 
 
• It is an influence that can change the state of motion of an object, measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• In base **SI units**, one **Newton** is equivalent to **1 kg×m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**:
 
 
• It refers to the rate of change of **displacement** in a specific direction.
 
• The standard **SI unit** for **velocity** is **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
 
 
• **Energy**:
 
 
• It represents the capacity for doing **work** and exists in various forms like **kinetic** and **potential energy**.
 
• The **SI unit** for **energy** is the **Joule (J)**, which is defined as **1 kg×m²/s²**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common symptom of diabetes mellitus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequent urination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diabetes mellitus** is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by **hyperglycemia**, where **blood glucose** levels remain consistently high due to either **insulin** deficiency or resistance.
 
• **Frequent urination**, medically termed **polyuria**, occurs when blood sugar levels exceed the **renal threshold**, which is typically around **180 mg/dL**.
 
• When the **kidneys** cannot reabsorb all the filtered glucose, the excess sugar is excreted into the urine; this creates an **osmotic gradient** that pulls large amounts of water from the body tissues, a process known as **osmotic diuresis**.
 
• The increased volume of urine leads to significant **dehydration**, which in turn triggers **polydipsia**, or extreme thirst, to compensate for the fluid loss.
 
• This symptom is one of the **'classic three'** early indicators of diabetes, alongside **polyphagia** (excessive hunger) and **polydipsia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Clarification of other symptoms and complications:
 
 
• **Polydipsia**: This is the medical term for **increased thirst**; it is a direct consequence of **polyuria** as the body seeks to restore **homeostasis** and fluid balance.
 
• **Hair loss**: Rather than increased hair growth, diabetics may experience **thinning hair** or **alopecia** due to poor **microcirculation** and **hormonal stress**.
 
• **Hearing impairment**: While not a primary diagnostic symptom, chronic **hyperglycemia** can damage the tiny blood vessels and nerves in the **inner ear** over time.
 
• **Type 1 vs. Type 2**: In **Type 1 diabetes**, the body produces no insulin (autoimmune), while in **Type 2**, the body becomes resistant to insulin; both result in **polyuria** as an early sign.
 
• **Ketones**: In some cases, high glucose levels lead to the production of **ketones**, which can be detected in the urine alongside sugar, indicating **diabetic ketoacidosis**.

questions.question: During the 17th BRICS Summit held in 2025, which country officially joined the bloc as a full member?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indonesia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **17th BRICS Summit** was hosted by **Brazil** in **2025**, following the **Russian Presidency** in **2024**. This summit served as a critical platform for formalizing the membership of countries that had previously expressed interest or held **Partner Country** status.
 
• **Indonesia**, the **largest economy in Southeast Asia** and a key member of **ASEAN**, officially joined the bloc as a full member during this summit. This move significantly bolstered the **Global South’s** representation within the group, reflecting **Indonesia’s** growing geopolitical and economic influence.
 
• The decision to join was accelerated under the administration of President **Prabowo Subianto**, who emphasized a **'non-aligned'** yet proactive foreign policy. By joining **BRICS**, **Indonesia** aimed to diversify its international partnerships and strengthen its voice in **global governance** reforms.
 
• The inclusion of **Indonesia** adds a massive consumer market and a resource-rich economy to the bloc, contributing to **BRICS** goals of **de-dollarization** and the use of **local currencies** in cross-border trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS Expansion Phases**:

 
 
• **Initial Expansion (2010)**: **South Africa** joined the original **BRIC** (Brazil, Russia, India, China) group.
 
• **Second Major Expansion (2024)**: At the beginning of **2024**, **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** became full members.
 
• **Partner Country Framework**: Introduced during the **16th Summit** in **Kazan (2024)**, this framework allowed nations like **Indonesia**, **Malaysia**, and **Vietnam** to engage with the bloc before full accession.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Impact**:
 
 
• **Indonesia’s GDP**: With a **GDP** exceeding **1 trillion USD**, **Indonesia** brings substantial economic weight, ranking among the top economies in the world by **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**.
 
• **Strategic Autonomy**: **Indonesia’s** membership is seen as a balancing act, as the country also pursues membership in the **OECD**, showcasing its intent to maintain **strategic autonomy** between different global economic clusters.

questions.question: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate is known for introducing the “Iqta system”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mamluk dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Iqta system** was a significant administrative and agrarian reform introduced in India by **Shams-ud-din Iltutmish**, who was the third ruler of the **Mamluk dynasty** (also known as the **Slave dynasty**), reigning from **1211 to 1236**.
 
• Under this system, the **Delhi Sultanate** was divided into various territorial units called **Iqtas**, which were assigned to military officers and nobles in place of cash salaries for their services to the state.
 
• The primary objective of introducing this system was to institutionalize the land revenue collection process and to provide a stable financial base for the standing army and the central bureaucracy.
 
• The holders of these land grants, known as **Iqtadars** or **Muqtis**, were tasked with collecting taxes from the peasants, maintaining law and order, and providing a stipulated number of troops to the **Sultan** during times of war.
 
• By introducing the **Iqta system**, **Iltutmish** successfully centralized the administration and integrated distant provinces into the **Delhi Sultanate**, effectively curbing the influence of local hereditary chieftains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilji dynasty**:

 
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** (1296−1316) introduced drastic reforms by converting small **Iqtas** into **Khalisa** (crown land) to bring revenue directly to the royal treasury.
 
• He abolished the intermediary roles of local officials like **Khuts** and **Muqaddams** to prevent tax evasion and corruption.
 
 
 
• **Tughlaq dynasty**:
 
 
• **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** reversed previous centralization efforts by making the **Iqta system** hereditary, which eventually weakened the central authority of the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• This period saw the proliferation of land grants to the **Ulema** and military officers as a means to secure political loyalty.
 
 
 
• **Sayyid dynasty**:
 
 
• Established by **Khizr Khan** in **1414**, this dynasty ruled over a much-diminished territory following the devastation caused by the invasion of **Timur** in **1398**.

questions.question: 'Bihu' is considered the festival of the ____________ state/UT.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihu** is the most significant socio-cultural festival of **Assam**, deeply intertwined with the state's agricultural calendar and ethnic identity.
 
• The festival is celebrated thrice a year, marking different stages of the **paddy cultivation** cycle.
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, also known as **Rongali Bihu**, is celebrated in mid-April. It marks the **Assamese New Year** and the arrival of the seeding season.
 
• **Magh Bihu**, or **Bhogali Bihu**, is observed in mid-January. It is a **harvest festival** characterized by community feasts and the burning of **Mejis** (structures made of bamboo and thatch).
 
• **Kati Bihu**, or **Kongali Bihu**, takes place in mid-October. It is a more solemn occasion involving the lighting of lamps to pray for a good harvest during the sapling growth phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Symbols of Assam**:

 
 
• **Bihu Dance**: A traditional folk dance performed by both men and women, featuring rapid hand movements and rhythmic swaying of the hips.
 
• **Gamosa**: A white rectangular piece of cloth with red borders, gifted during **Bihu** as a mark of respect and affection.
 
• **Musical Instruments**: The celebrations feature the **Dhol** (drum), **Pepa** (horn made from buffalo horn), **Gogona**, and **Taal**.
 
 
 
• **Other States/UTs**:
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**: Known for the **Island Tourism Festival** and various tribal celebrations.
 
• **Chhattisgarh**: Notable for festivals like **Bastar Dussehra**, **Hareli**, and **Madai**.
 
• **Lakshadweep**: Major festivals include **Eid-ul-Fitr**, **Bakrid**, and **Milad-un-Nabi**, reflecting its unique cultural heritage.

questions.question: Which function is primarily handled by system software in a computer system?

options.text: Coordinating hardware and running core system processes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coordinating hardware and running core system processes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **System Software** refers to the collection of programs that manage and support the computer system's resources and operations, acting as a bridge between the **Hardware** and **Application Software**.
 
• A primary example of system software is the **Operating System (OS)**, which is responsible for **Processor Management**. It uses scheduling algorithms to allocate **CPU** time to various tasks, ensuring the system remains responsive.
 
• **Hardware Coordination** is achieved through **Device Drivers** and **Firmware**, which provide the necessary instructions for the OS to communicate with peripheral devices like **Graphics Cards**, **Hard Drives**, and **Input/Output devices**.
 
• **Core System Processes** involve critical background functions such as **Memory Management**, which monitors **RAM** usage, and **File System Management**, which controls how data is stored and retrieved from the disk using structures like **NTFS** or **ext4**.
 
• Unlike application software, which is triggered by user demand, system software usually starts during the **Booting Process** (via the **BIOS/UEFI**) and runs continuously to maintain the stability and integrity of the entire computational environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Application Software**:

 
 
• These are programs designed to perform specific user-centric tasks. Examples include **Media Players** (playing audio/video), **Word Processors** (managing documents), and **Spreadsheet Software** (designing data sheets).
 
• They do not have direct access to the **Hardware**; instead, they make requests to the system software to use system resources.
 
 
 
• **Language Translators**:
 
 
• Considered a type of system software, **Compilers**, **Interpreters**, and **Assemblers** translate high-level programming languages into **Machine Code** that the **Central Processing Unit** can execute.
 
 
 
• **Utility Software**:
 
 
• Often bundled with the OS, utilities include **Disk Defragmenters**, **Encryption Tools**, and **Antivirus Software**, which help in the maintenance, optimization, and protection of the computer system.

questions.question: According to the Natyashastra, which of the following is characterised by body movements to music without expressions (Abhinay)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nritta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nritta** is defined in the **Natyashastra**, an ancient Sanskrit treatise attributed to **Sage Bharata**, as a form of 'pure dance' that focuses on rhythmic precision and technical virtuosity.
 
• It is characterized by the absence of **Abhinaya** (mimetic expression), meaning the dancer does not attempt to convey a specific story, sentiment, or thematic narrative through facial expressions.
 
• The performance is composed of **Karanas** (basic dance units) and **Angaharas** (combinations of Karanas) that emphasize the aesthetic beauty of the human form in motion.
 
• The movements in **Nritta** are strictly governed by **Tala** (rhythmic cycles) and **Laya** (tempo), utilizing footwork and stylized hand gestures solely for decorative and rhythmic purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nritya**:

 
 
• Unlike Nritta, **Nritya** is an expressive dance form that combines rhythmic movement with **Abhinaya**.
 
• It aims to evoke **Rasa** (aesthetic flavor) in the audience by portraying **Bhavas** (emotions) and specific meanings through hand gestures and facial movements.
 
 
 
• **Natya**:
 
 
• This term refers to the dramatic element or the **theatrical aspect** of a performance.
 
• It involves a plot, characters, and often **Vachika Abhinaya** (speech or dialogue) to enact a full story or play.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**:
 
 
• A classical dance form originating from **Andhra Pradesh**, which integrates all three elements: **Nritta**, **Nritya**, and **Natya**.
 
• It is well-known for its **Tarangam** segment, where the dancer performs while balancing on the edges of a **brass plate**.

questions.question: Which resolution is the Preamble of the Constitution based on, drafted by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Objectives Resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Objectives Resolution** was a historic document moved by **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru** in the **Constituent Assembly** on **December 13, 1946**, which provided the ideological basis for the Constitution.
 
• It laid down the fundamentals and philosophy of the constitutional structure, envisioning India as an **Independent Sovereign Republic** where all power and authority are derived from the **people**.
 
• The resolution guaranteed to all Indian citizens **social, economic, and political justice**; **equality of status and opportunity**; and **freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship**.
 
• It included specific safeguards for **minorities, backward and tribal areas**, and **depressed and other backward classes** to ensure inclusive democratic development.
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** unanimously adopted the resolution on **January 22, 1947**, and its essence was subsequently distilled into the **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution with minor modifications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**:

 
 
• These are enshrined in **Part III** of the Constitution (Articles 12 − 35).
 
• They are **justiciable** in nature and are meant for promoting the ideal of political democracy.
 
• The concept was inspired by the **Bill of Rights** of the **USA**.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**:
 
 
• These are enumerated in **Part IV** (Articles 36 − 51) and were borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• They are **non-justiciable** but are fundamental in the governance of the country, aimed at establishing a **welfare state**.
 
 
 
• **The Preamble**:
 
 
• It serves as the **identity card** of the Constitution, reflecting its spirit and objectives.
 
• It was amended by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, which added three new words: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.

• The **Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)** was established under **Article 323A** of the **Constitution of India**, a provision added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, to adjudicate disputes regarding the recruitment and conditions of service of public servants.

questions.question:
Which statement is True or False about the first and second generations of computers?

(ii) The Transistor, which defined the Second Generation, made computers larger, slower, and more expensive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) True, (ii) False**__.

• The **First Generation of Computers** (roughly **1940−1956**) relied on **Vacuum Tubes** for circuitry and **Magnetic Drums** for memory. These machines, such as the **ENIAC** and **UNIVAC**, were physically massive, often occupying entire rooms, and generated extreme amounts of **heat**, which frequently caused hardware failures. Hence, statement (i) is correct.
 
• The **Second Generation of Computers** (roughly **1956−1963**) was characterized by the replacement of vacuum tubes with the **Transistor**. This technological shift did not make computers larger or slower; rather, it allowed them to become significantly **smaller**, **faster**, **cheaper**, and more **energy-efficient** than their predecessors. Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation (Vacuum Tubes)**:

 
 
• These computers used **Machine Language** (binary code) for programming.
 
• They were extremely **expensive** to operate and consumed vast amounts of **electricity**.
 
• The **ENIAC** contained approximately 18,000 vacuum tubes and weighed over 30 tons.
 
 
 
• **Second Generation (Transistors)**:
 
 
• The **Transistor** was invented at **Bell Labs** in **1947** but saw widespread use in computers in the mid-1950s.
 
• This era saw the development of early **high-level programming languages** like **COBOL** and **FORTRAN**.
 
• Computers moved from using magnetic drums to **magnetic core technology** for primary memory.

questions.question: What is the term used for the first matra in Hindustani music’s tala system?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Hindustani Classical Music**, a **Tala** is a rhythmic cycle characterized by a specific number of **Matras** (beats) and **Vibhags** (divisions).
 
• The **first matra** of any tala cycle is fundamentally termed **Sam**, which serves as the primary point of resolution and maximum rhythmic emphasis.
 
• **Sam** acts as the essential junction where the main performer (vocalist or instrumentalist) and the percussionist (usually playing the **Tabla** or **Pakhawaj**) meet to conclude a rhythmic pattern or melodic phrase.
 
• In the standardized **Bhatkhande Notation System**, the **Sam** is denoted by the symbol **'X'**, distinguishing it from other accented or unaccented beats.
 
• The arrival at **Sam** signifies the completion of one **Avartan** (full cycle) and the simultaneous commencement of the next, maintaining the structural continuity of the **Raga** performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khali**:

 
 
• The term literally translates to **'empty'** and refers to a specific beat in a tala cycle that is marked by a wave of the hand rather than a clap.
 
• In notation, it is represented by the symbol **'0'** and serves to provide a structural counter-balance to the **Sam** and **Tali**.
 
 
 
• **Tali**:
 
 
• This term refers to the **claps** used to mark the beginning of various **Vibhags** within a tala, excluding the **Khali**.
 
• It helps performers navigate complex rhythmic structures, such as **Teental** (16 beats) or **Jhaptal** (10 beats), by identifying internal subdivisions.
 
 
 
• **Laya**:
 
 
• **Laya** refers to the **tempo** or the speed at which the tala cycle is executed.
 
• It is categorized into three primary levels: **Vilambit** (slow), **Madhya** (medium), and **Drut** (fast), each dictating the mood and complexity of the musical composition.

• This property ensures that the machine can operate **24/7** for days or even years (as seen in **servers** and **supercomputers**) without requiring a break, provided the **hardware components** and **power supply** remain stable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Two isotopes of an element have 17 protons with 18 neutrons and 20 neutrons, respectively. Which of the following is the correct representation of these isotopes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**³⁵₁₇Cl and ³⁷₁₇Cl**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atomic Number (Z)** of an element is defined as the total number of **protons** present in the nucleus of its atom. In this problem, the element has **17 protons**, which identifies it as **Chlorine (Cl)**.
 
• The **Mass Number (A)** is the sum of the number of **protons** and **neutrons** (collectively called **nucleons**) in the nucleus. It is expressed by the formula: **A = Z + n**, where **n** is the number of neutrons.
 
• For the first isotope, the mass number is calculated as **17 (protons) + 18 (neutrons) = 35**. Thus, its mass number is **35**.
 
• For the second isotope, the mass number is calculated as **17 (protons) + 20 (neutrons) = 37**. Thus, its mass number is **37**.
 
• In chemical notation, an isotope is represented as **AZX**, where the **Mass Number (A)** is written as a **superscript** and the **Atomic Number (Z)** is written as a **subscript** to the left of the chemical symbol **X**.
 
• By substituting the values, we get the two isotopes as **³⁵₁₇Cl** and **³⁷₁₇Cl**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes**:

 
 
• Isotopes are atoms of the **same element** that have the same number of **protons** but a different number of **neutrons**.
 
• They possess identical **chemical properties** because they have the same **electronic configuration** and number of valence electrons.
 
• They exhibit different **physical properties**, such as density and boiling points, due to the variation in their **atomic masses**.
 
 
 
• **Average Atomic Mass**:
 
 
• Naturally occurring **Chlorine** is a mixture of its isotopes. **Chlorine-35** and **Chlorine-37** occur in a ratio of approximately **3:1** (**75%** and **25%** respectively).
 
• The **average atomic mass** of Chlorine is calculated as a weighted average, resulting in the value of **35.5 u**, which is why many periodic tables do not show a whole number for its mass.
 
 
 
• **Other Examples**:
 
 
• **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium (¹H)**, **Deuterium (²H)**, and **Tritium (³H)**.
 
• **Carbon** isotopes include **Carbon-12** (stable), **Carbon-13**, and **Carbon-14** (used in radiocarbon dating).

• **Brahui** is a member of the **North Dravidian** language family, primarily spoken by the **Brahui people** in the **Balochistan** province of **Pakistan**.
 
• It is the only **Dravidian language** spoken almost entirely outside the **Indian subcontinent** proper, situated approximately 1,500 kilometers away from the main cluster of **Dravidian** languages in **Southern India**.
 
• Beyond **Pakistan**, significant speaker populations are found in **Southern Afghanistan** and the **Sistan and Baluchestan** province of **Iran**.

questions.question: After gaining Independence, what type of economic system did India implement as its development strategy?

options.text: Free market capitalism with minimal state intervention
Mixed economy combining public and private sectors
Traditional agrarian structure without structural reforms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixed economy combining public and private sectors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Following **Independence** in **1947**, India adopted a **Mixed Economic System** to balance the dual goals of rapid economic growth and **social justice**.
 
• This model was championed by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who believed that the state must control the **commanding heights** of the economy to ensure equitable distribution of wealth.
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948** officially laid the foundation for this system, dividing industries into those reserved for the **public sector** and those open to the **private sector**.
 
• Under this strategy, the **Government of India** took responsibility for **heavy industries**, **infrastructure**, and **social services**, while leaving **agriculture** and **consumer goods** largely to private enterprise.
 
• The implementation was managed through **centralized planning**, leading to the establishment of the **Planning Commission** in **1950** and the launch of the **First Five-Year Plan** in **1951**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Ideologies Comparison:**

 
 
• **Free Market Capitalism:** This was rejected because the **private sector** at the time lacked sufficient **capital** and **technology** to build the massive infrastructure required for a newly independent nation.
 
• **Socialist System:** While influenced by **Soviet planning**, India did not adopt a total **communist/socialist** model (eliminating private property) to uphold **democratic principles** and individual freedom.
 
• **License-Permit Raj:** To regulate the **private sector** within the mixed economy, the government introduced strict **licensing** under the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951**.
 
• **Mahalanobis Model:** The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)** shifted focus toward **capital-intensive heavy industries** to achieve **self-reliance** and **import substitution**.

questions.question: Tropical cyclones form mainly due to:

options.text: Low-pressure systems over warm ocean water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low-pressure systems over warm ocean water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical cyclones** are intense **low-pressure systems** that develop over tropical or subtropical waters, characterized by a closed atmospheric circulation and strong winds.
 
• The primary engine for these storms is the **latent heat of condensation**; as warm, moist air rises from the ocean surface, it cools and condenses into clouds, releasing energy that fuels the storm.
 
• A critical requirement for formation is a **sea surface temperature (SST)** of at least **26.5°C** (approximately 80°F) reaching down to a depth of about **50 meters**.
 
• The **Coriolis force** is necessary to provide the rotation required for the storm to spin; because this force is zero at the equator, tropical cyclones typically form between **5° and 30° latitude**.
 
• These systems are known by different names based on their location: **Hurricanes** in the North Atlantic and Eastern Pacific, **Typhoons** in the Northwest Pacific, and **Cyclones** in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-pressure systems over land**:

 
 
• These systems, also called **anticyclones**, generally bring stable, clear weather and sinking air, which inhibits the vertical cloud growth necessary for cyclone development.
 
 
 
• **Rising continental winds**:
 
 
• While rising air (convection) occurs over land, **continents** do not provide the massive, sustained supply of moisture found over oceans required to maintain a tropical cyclone's intensity.
 
 
 
• **Fast-moving cold fronts**:
 
 
• Cold fronts are characteristic of **extratropical cyclones** (mid-latitude storms) rather than tropical ones; tropical cyclones are **warm-core systems** that thrive on heat rather than temperature gradients between air masses.
 
 
 
• **Vertical Wind Shear**:
 
 
• A **low vertical wind shear** is essential for formation; strong winds at higher altitudes can tilt or disrupt the storm's structure, preventing it from organizing.

questions.question: Which type of Emergency could be implemented due to 'internal disturbance' before the 44th Amendment of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Emergency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 352** of the Indian Constitution, the **President of India** can declare a **National Emergency** when the security of India or any part of it is threatened by **war**, **external aggression**, or **internal disturbance**.
 
• The phrase **'internal disturbance'** was part of the original constitutional text since its adoption in **1950**, providing a broad and somewhat vague ground for the executive to assume extraordinary powers.
 
• This specific provision was famously utilized by the **Indira Gandhi**-led government to proclaim a **National Emergency** on **June 25, 1975**, which lasted for 21 months until **1977**.
 
• To prevent the potential misuse of this term in the future, the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**, introduced by the **Janata Government**, replaced 'internal disturbance' with the more specific term **'armed rebellion'**.
 
• The amendment ensured that a **National Emergency** could no longer be declared merely on the grounds of political instability or non-violent protests, requiring a higher threshold of domestic violence involving arms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President's Rule**:

 
 
• Governed by **Article 356**, it is imposed when a **State Government** cannot function according to constitutional provisions.
 
• It is also known as **State Emergency** or **Constitutional Emergency**.
 
 
 
• **Financial Emergency**:
 
 
• Authorized under **Article 360**, it can be declared if the **financial stability** or credit of India is under threat.
 
• Notably, this type of emergency has **never been declared** in the history of independent India.
 
 
 
• **Martial Law**:
 
 
• Referenced in **Article 34**, it involves the **suspension of ordinary law** and the administration of justice by military tribunals in specific areas.
 
• Unlike a **National Emergency**, there is no specific provision in the Constitution that defines the exact grounds for its declaration.

• Modern communication networks, including **telecom and high-speed internet**, facilitate real-time business transactions, **e-commerce**, and digital banking, which are fundamental to a modern **service-oriented economy**.

• Launched to provide **multi-modal connectivity** infrastructure to various economic zones.
 
• Aims to break silos between departments and ensure holistic planning for **logistical efficiency**.

• A centrally-sponsored umbrella program focusing on optimizing the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across the country by bridging critical **infrastructure gaps**.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Programme**:
 
 
• A flagship program to transform India into a **digitally empowered society**, significantly boosting the communication infrastructure required for **FinTech** and **knowledge-based industries**.

• Infrastructure prevents **regional isolation** by integrating rural and remote areas into the mainstream market, promoting **balanced regional growth** and poverty reduction.
